steps.note: Create the RFQ used for the bid-expiry scenario.
Configure the event as an RFQ rather than the default auction.
Apply an RFQ pricing template before adding line items.
Add the product that will appear in the vendor bid sheet.
Complete the RFQ pricing sheet so the event can be published.
Commit the shortest supported event duration; the exact one-minute setup is not expressible.
Invite the QA vendor who will attempt the expired bid.
Publish the RFQ before opening it in the vendor portal.
Confirm the event reached a real published project page.
Move to the separate vendor session while keeping the buyer session available.
Open the live RFQ's pricing sheet as the invited vendor.
Return to the buyer session to let the event countdown expire.
Wait for the bidding window to end rather than force-ending it.
Return to the vendor's already opened RFQ after expiry.
Attempt to submit after the countdown; this passes only if the portal refuses the bid or keeps submission disabled.
Check the buyer-side response record after the refused submission.
Verify that no vendor response was recorded.
